cues.en: This is woodblock printmaker David Ball speaking to you from my carving bench temporarily located in one corner of our new shop in Asakusa. It's evening now and with the front door locked and nobody else coming up the stairs to bother me I can get started on the evenings work. This may be my carving bench but as you can see it's not a woodblock that I'm working on tonight it's a tablet and my laptop. My carving tools are tucked away in their box and I have a plastic pen instead.
cues.zh: 我是木版画师 David Ball，现在我们在浅草新店一角的临时雕刻台前向大家问好。现在已经是晚上了，前门已锁，也不会有人上楼来打扰，我终于可以开始今晚的工作了。这里虽然是我的雕刻台，但如大家所见，我今晚处理的并不是木版，而是一块数位板和笔记本电脑。我的雕刻刀都收在盒子里，手里拿的则是一支塑料触控笔。

cues.en: This isn't exactly what they used in the old days to make prints, of course, but it's going to play a very important role in my next job, which is, as you have probably guessed, the carving of a set of blocks for our new edition of Hokusai's Great Wave image. This is going to be a reproduction, of course, and that means I need a master copy to work from.
cues.zh: 当然，这显然不是古人制作版画用的工具，但它在我接下来的工作中会起到非常关键的作用——大家可能已经猜到了，就是为我们新版的北斋《巨浪》雕刻一套印版。当然，这是一次复刻，也就是说我需要一份用于参考的原作底稿。

cues.en: A poor printmaker like myself can't possibly afford to get his hands on an original, but in truth, just what constitutes an original of this design is pretty much up in the air. This image has been recut and republished and reprinted literally dozens of times over the years, even beginning back in the Edo and Meiji periods, when there was of course no such concept as copyright. Prints in museums now that are well over 100 years old are just as likely to be reproductions, or at best, late copies from the early block sets.
cues.zh: 像我这样囊中羞涩的版画家显然买不起原版，但坦白讲，这幅画究竟怎样才算“原版”其实根本没有定论。多年来，这幅画作被重刻、再版、重印了不下几十次，甚至早在江户和明治时代就开始了，而那时当然根本没有版权的概念。如今博物馆里那些有一百多年历史的版画，也极有可能只是复刻品，或者充其量是用早期印版在后期印制出来的版本。

cues.en: Scholars and academics argue to let cows come home over any given copy. How early is this one? Is this an original? Me, I don't know. And I don't care. Now before you panic and start to wonder just what kind of print I'll be making here, let me explain how I'm going to approach this. Any number of museums and collections now have images of this print available online. And I myself have collected a number of copies of the print. I'm going to study these and I'm going to use as my guide the prints
cues.zh: 学者和专家们对任何一件作品都能争论个没完。这幅版画有多古老？这是一幅原作吗？至于我，我不知道。我也不在乎。大家先别慌，也别琢磨我到底会在这里做什么印品，听我解释一下我将如何处理这件事。现在很多博物馆和收藏机构的官网上都能找到这幅版画的图像。我自己也收集了这幅版画的多个版本。我要对这些版本进行研究，并且把那些

cues.en: plural, that is, that when you drill down, show the most artistry in their production. Let me show you what I mean with images of a copy in the Smithsonian Museum and of a print currently available here in Tokyo. To start with, I'm going to focus on this area just under the crest of the wave. There shouldn't really be much difference in these prints, should there? After all, they were made by the same kind of carvers and the same kind of printers, trained in the same traditions, working with the same goal in mind.
cues.zh: 复数形式的版本——也就是说，当你深入观察时，在制作上展现出最高艺术水准的版本——作为我的参考指南。让我用史密森尼博物馆藏品的图像以及目前在东京能买到的一幅版画，来向大家展示我的意思。首先，我把重点放在浪尖下方这片区域。这些版画之间其实不该有太大差异，对吧？毕竟，它们是由同一类雕刻师和同一类印刷师制作的，受过相同的传统训练，带着相同的目标进行创作。

cues.en: Here's the old museum copy. There's a little bit of misregistration as some of the wave outlines don't quite match up with the color areas. But other than that, it shows a very good palette. The different shades of blue work together quite well. And look at the lines. Each and every line shows the original character of the brush strokes. The overall appearance is very pleasing and it's wonderfully done. And this is the modern one. I'm not sure what to say other than, my god, they actually sell this.
cues.zh: 这是老旧的博物馆藏本。有一些套色不准的问题，因为有些浪花的轮廓与颜色区域没有完全对齐。但除此之外，它展现出了非常棒的色彩搭配。不同深浅的蓝色搭配得相当和谐。再看看这些线条。每一条线都展现出了笔触原有的质感。整体外观非常赏心悦目，完成度极高。而这是现代的版本。除了“天哪，这居然也有人买”之外，我真不知道该说些什么好。

cues.en: It isn't just misregistered. Those colouraries don't even remotely match the bounding lines and the choice of pigments and tints. You don't have to be a connoisseur of Japanese art to see that something is very wrong here. It's well done printing in the sense that the printer has put the colours down smoothly, but there's just no taste at work here. These people either don't know or don't care what constitutes real Japanese printmaking. Anyway, enough of that. Anybody can look good when compared with stuff like that.
cues.zh: 这不仅仅是对位不准。那些副色调甚至跟边界线完全对不上，颜料和色调的选择也很糟糕。你根本不需要是什么日本艺术鉴赏家，也能看出这里面问题很大。从印刷工把颜色铺得很平滑这个角度来说，它印得挺好，但这里面完全没有品味可言。这些人要么不知道，要么根本不在乎真正的日本版画到底是什么样的。好了，这个就说到这儿。跟这种东西一比，任何人都能显得很优秀。

cues.en: My point in showing you that one was simply to illustrate my approach. For the first stage of production, I need a clear set of line work, the main outlines of the design elements. I'm going to trace those from that Smithsonian copy. The misregistration you saw there is of no consequence. It's the lines themselves that I'm interested in. They show taste and style. That carver knew what he was doing. So that's where this tablet and computer come in.
cues.zh: 我给你们看那个的意图，只是为了说明我的方法。在制作的第一阶段，我需要一套清晰的线条稿，也就是设计元素的主轮廓。我会从史密森尼的那份复制品上把它们临摹下来。你刚才看到的对位不准根本不重要。我感兴趣的是线条本身。它们展现出了品味和风格。那个雕刻师是个行家。所以，这就轮到这台平板电脑和电脑派上用场了。

cues.en: I have brought the image into Photoshop and I'm tracing each and every line of the print onto a fresh layer in order to separate them from the colors that they were printed with. Once I have the outlines isolated and thus clearly visible, I will then be able to transfer them to the woodblock and get carving. Here's how I'm going to do it. This is a view of my Photoshop screen. I know it's very enlarged and you can see in places where I've now begun to trace on a separate layer with my pen.
cues.zh: 我把图像导入了 Photoshop，正在把版画的每一条线都描摹到一个新的图层上，以便将它们与原本印刷的颜色分离开来。一旦我把轮廓分离出来并能清晰可见，我就可以把它们转移到木板上开始雕刻了。我是这么操作的。这是我的 Photoshop 屏幕视图。我知道它放大得很大，你可以在某些地方看到我刚刚开始用画笔在一个单独的图层上进行描摹。

cues.en: I'm tracing it red so that we can see clearly what I'm doing. Each and every line I'm trying to go over it, catch the thin parts, the thick parts and try and get as much as I can the original flavour of those lines. Now it's sometimes a bit difficult actually to see what I'm doing even though it's partly transparent. So underneath the red layer I've put another layer in of blank white. So now and then as I go over each line what I do I then click the white layer up and that allows me to see the shape of the lines I've drawn. I can then
cues.zh: 我正在用红色描线，这样我们能看清我在做什么。每一根线条我都试着描一遍，抓住细的部分、粗的部分，尽量保留这些线条原本的韵味。不过有时候即使线条部分是透明的，也不太容易看清我在做什么。所以在红色图层下面，我又加了一层纯白色。这样每描完一根线条，我就会把白色图层调上来，这样就能看清我画的线条的形状。然后我可以

cues.en: As I'm doing here I can then pad it out a bit, switch to an eraser, scrape it off a bit. I can end up with a line that looks really nice and juicy and ready for carving. I can put the original back there and of course I can click off the red layer again anytime I want to see the actual original lines. And I go over the whole entire print this way. It's going to take me quite a few days. So there we are and all pen to paper as it were and production of our print is now underway.
cues.zh: 就像我现在做的，我可以把它稍微加粗一点，切换到橡皮擦，稍微刮掉一些。最后我就能得到一条看起来又漂亮又饱满、可以开始雕刻的线条。我可以把原稿放回去，当然我随时可以关掉红色图层，去看真正的原始线条。我就这样把整幅版画都描一遍。这要花我好几天时间。好了，就这样，可以说全是笔和纸的活儿，我们的版画制作现在已经开始了。

cues.en: The next video in this set will show how I get the image from this machine over onto an actual wood block and then of course we'll begin carving. Before I close this episode off though, I think it might be interesting if I put my jacket on and we take a short walk together. Let's go outside.
cues.zh: 这一系列的下一个视频会展示我如何把图像从这台机器上转到真正的木版上，然后当然我们就开始雕刻了。不过在结束这一集之前，我觉得穿上我的夹克，我们一起短途散个步可能会挺有意思。我们出去吧。

cues.en: Here we are outside the shop. It's a fairly quiet Sunday evening. It's about seven o'clock and it's about time for me to think about dinner. But before I decide where to go, let's take a little walk around the neighborhood here and see some of the sights. We'll start by going around the corner to the famous Hopi Dori. This one is really quiet tonight. The last few days it's been the New Year's season here. It's been just buzzing and it's settled down now this Sunday night. I don't think I'll be choosing one of these for my own dinner tonight. They're a little bit touristy. Let's head a bit more closer towards Sensoji Temple.
cues.zh: 我们现在在店外面。这是一个相当安静的周日傍晚。大约七点钟，我也该想想晚饭吃什么了。不过在我决定去哪儿之前，咱们先在附近的街区随便走走，看几个景点。我们先拐个弯去著名的法善寺横丁。这里今晚真的很安静。过去几天这里正好是新年假期。之前一直热闹非凡，现在这个周日晚上终于安静下来了。我想今晚我不会在这里选地方吃晚饭。这些地方稍微有点游客化。我们再往浅草寺那边走近一点。

cues.en: There's one of the gable ends of San Soji Temple behind me and boy, you should have seen this place the last few days, the New Year's season. People praying at the temple then pouring out through these gates coming down here. We could not have stood here like this and done this. Let's go a bit closer. I'm going to stay behind the camera here for the next bit because you don't need to see my face and anyway I've got to guide the camera. There's the temple seen from this corner. There's still trucks here, they're cleaning up some of the leftovers from the New Year festival. That's the sky tree in the background.
cues.zh: 我身后就是浅草寺的一个山墙，天哪，你要是看看这地方过去几天的元旦假期是什么样就好了。人们在寺里祈祷，然后从这些大门涌出来走到这里。我们刚才可没法像这样站在这儿拍视频。咱们再走近一点。接下来的时间我会留在镜头后面，因为你们不需要看我的脸，而且总归我要扶着镜头。从这个角落看过去的寺庙。这里还有卡车，他们在清理新年庙会留下的一些垃圾。背景里那个是晴空塔。

cues.en: and swinging around you can see part of the spotlights they've really done a beautiful job on the illumination here that's the smaller gate just in front of San Soji and then the real what do we call the real thing to see is up on the front of his there's the five-story pagoda and they've done such a beautiful job with the illuminations I don't know if this camera is going to catch it but it looks just so good let's move over out front of the main temple
cues.zh: 转过镜头，你能看到部分聚光灯，这里的灯光效果真的做得太漂亮了，那是浅草寺正前方较小的那座门，然后真正的主角——我们怎么说呢，真正值得一看的是正前方那座五重塔，这里的灯光照明真的做得太棒了，我不知道这个摄像机能不能拍出效果，但看起来实在是太赞了，咱们移步到正殿前面去吧

cues.en: You know, I really honestly don't have much interest in the religious aspects of a place like this, but it's clearly an important part of Japanese culture. And to be living, you know, 60 seconds, come out of my front door, and one minute later, I'm standing here, it's just so cool, I can't actually believe it's actually happening. A last shot of the temple here before we head off in another direction, and of course, again, the beautiful pagoda. The temple is now behind the camera, we're facing the other way, and this is the top end of the famous Nakamise.
cues.zh: 你知道吗，老实说我对这种地方的宗教方面其实没什么兴趣，但这显然是日本文化中很重要的一部分。而且能住在这里，你知道的，出门走60秒，走出我家前门，一分钟后我就能站在这里，这实在是太酷了，我简直不敢相信这是真的。在转向另一个方向之前，这是寺庙的最后几个镜头，当然，还有那座美丽的五重塔。寺庙现在已经在镜头背后了，我们面向相反的方向，这里就是著名的仲见世街的最北端。

cues.en: the street of shops that runs up from the main street towards the temple. We're about a third of the way down, the Nakamise, the famous street, but we're going to turn off here because on the right-hand side, this is where it joins the famous Dempoindori. And there's a destination along here that I don't want to miss. These shopkeepers along this part of Dempoindori have done a really nice job making their street attractive to passers-by, but it's the next block that I'm more interested in right now. Let's go.
cues.zh: 这条商业街从主干道一直通往寺庙。我们大概走了三分之一，这里就是著名的仲见世街（Nakamise），不过我们要在前面拐弯了，因为右手边连着著名的传法院通（Dempoindori）。沿着这条街有个地方我绝不能错过。传法院通这一带的店家花了不少心思吸引过往行人，但我现在更感兴趣的是下一个街区。我们走吧。

cues.en: Yes, you might recognize where we are. We've come around full circle. This is Dokkodori and just down on the left hand side there's a certain mocha hunk on print shop. I'm now going to drop off the camera, head out for dinner and pack it up for the night. Thank you very much for watching so far. It shouldn't be long now before I bring you part two of this set of videos documenting the production of the Great Wave print. See you next time. Thank you and good night.
cues.zh: 没错，大家可能认出这是哪儿了。我们绕了一大圈又回来了。这里是 Dokkodori，顺着往前走左手边，就是那家 Mokuhankan 版画店。我现在准备收工放下相机，去吃晚饭，今天就拍到这里了。非常感谢大家一路收看。应该很快就会为大家带来记录《神奈川冲浪里》版画制作过程的第二期视频。我们下期再见。谢谢，晚安。
